examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}は{赤字|あかじ}になった。
examples.english: We went into the red this year.

examples.japanese: {赤字|あかじ}を{減|へ}らす{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: We need to reduce the deficit.

examples.japanese: {家計|かけい}が{赤字|あかじ}だ。
examples.english: The household budget is in the red.

notes:
{赤字|あかじ} literally means "red characters" because losses were traditionally written in red ink.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {赤字|あかじ}になる (to go into the red)
- {赤字|あかじ}が{出|で}る (to incur a loss)
- {赤字|あかじ}を{出|だ}す (to run a deficit)
- {赤字|あかじ}{経営|けいえい} (operating at a loss)
- {赤字|あかじ}{決算|けっさん} (deficit settlement)
- {財政|ざいせい}{赤字|あかじ} (fiscal deficit)

CONTEXTS:
- {企業|きぎょう}の{赤字|あかじ} (corporate loss)
- {国|くに}の{財政|ざいせい}{赤字|あかじ} (national fiscal deficit)
- {家計|かけい}の{赤字|あかじ} (household budget deficit)
- {貿易|ぼうえき}{赤字|あかじ} (trade deficit)

ANTONYM:
- {黒字|くろじ} (surplus, in the black)
